 By the time its series finale aired in 2004, Frasier had accomplished a rare feat. Clocking in at 11 seasons, the Cheers spinoff lived a life that was equally as long as its predecessor. When the show was rebooted in 2023, Kelsey Grammer had officially been playing Frasier for 40 years , another unprecedented milestone for the series.

 Notably, though, the cast of the Frasier reboot featured hardly any of the show's original players. John Mahoney, who played Martin Crane, passed in 2018, while Niles' David Hyde Pierce and Daphne's Jane Leeves declined to return. Only Peri Gilpin made an appearance, playing Roz in a limited capacity, leaving Grammer surrounded by an otherwise entirely new cast.
 This left the 2023 Frasier somewhere between a nostalgic revival and an entirely new series. This disconnect, spurred by the absence of much of the original cast, likely played a major role in the new Frasier 's cancellation after just two seasons .
 While the reboot's performance underscores the magic of Frasier ​​​​​​'s original cast, it also reveals a road not taken. Instead of reviving Grammer's original Frasier Crane over 20 years later, the series could have been given a fresh start by reimagining the original story with a completely new cast. If this were a direction Frasier ​​​​​​were to go, these would be the actors for the job.
 Danny McBride
 As Frasier Crane
 The Righteous Gemstones' Danny McBride as Jesse Gemstone Image via HBO 
 Danny McBride's The Righteous Gemstones couldn't be more different from Frasier , yet his performance in the HBO hit made a surprisingly strong case for how the actor would fare as Frasier. Kelsey Grammer's Frasier was posh and reluctant to get his hands dirty with the less-than-finer things in life, yet he fancied himself a capable, even rugged man. Compared to Niles, this may have even been true.
 This description also largely applies to McBride's Jesse Gemstone, the eldest brother in the show's megachurch family who constantly sought to prove himself capable in a world he had spent his life being insulated from. In doing so, Jesse often found himself raising his voice, yet McBride managed to capture the farce of the volume without the aggression, another prominent trait of Frasier's.
 Chris Perfetti
 As Niles Crane
 Jacob Hill in a classroom in Abbott Elementary season 4 
 David Hyde Pierce found a one-of-a-kind rhythm as Frasier's even more neurotic, yet somehow more emotionally resonant brother. Frasier's elegant condo and particular way of living in it seemed excessive until viewers were introduced to Niles' massive, gothic castle of an estate, complete with a staff. Even swathed in the stiff excess, though, Niles' emotions were palpable and genuine.
 With his work on Abbott Elementary and DTF St. Louis , Chris Perfetti has delivered similar performances, proving that he can balance perfectly timed line delivery, delicate physical comedy, and more earnestness than viewers would expect from the characters he's played. ​​​​​​​Anyone stepping into this role would have big shoes to fill, but Perfetti would bring his own unique charm to the character.
 Eugene Levy
 As Martin Crane
 Eugene Levy as Johnny Rose talking on the phone in Schitt's Creek 
 The retired cop with distinctly blue-collar energy may seem like an interesting choice for the actor now famous for playing Schitt's Creek ​​​​​​'s formerly wealthy patriarch. However, what Eugene Levy actually accomplished in that role and others throughout his career is playing the down-to-earth straight man to an otherwise eccentric ensemble, and that is exactly what the character of Martin functions as.
 As Frasier and Niles got each other preoccupied with proving increasingly petty points, John Mahoney's Martin was there to drink beer, watch football, and offer life lessons about the things that truly matter in life. The late Mahoney was quick, blunt, and got plenty of laughs of his own, though none of this is out of reach for Levy, a comedic talent of a generation.
 Rachel Sennott
 As Roz Doyle
 Rachel Sennott in I Love LA Season 1 Image via MovieStillsDB 
 Roz was a unique female character for a '90s sitcom. Her primary characteristic was frequent and tumultuous escapades with men, yet these happened largely off-screen, as she was seen almost exclusively at work. Peri Gilpin's performance added to the character's uniqueness, as she was effortlessly dry and capable of going toe-to-toe with Frasier with a loving dismissiveness that few could pull off.

 Very few sitcoms have had writing as sharp as Frasier, or a cast as talented and hilarious, so the show is jam-packed with quotable one-liners.

 By  
 Ben Sherlock 
 Rachel Sennott, too, has proven herself an abundantly capable comedic mind. Most recently, she created I Love LA , an HBO comedy where she plays a long-suffering assistant whose competent, straight-faced way of dealing with her boss rivals the Roz and Frasier dynamic. Sennott may well bring her trademark " Valley Girl " dialect to the role, but in 2026, that just might work.
 Juno Temple
 As Daphne Moon
 Roy, Keeley, and Jamie in Ted Lasso 
 Martin's British, whimsical, carefree, spiritual live-in physical therapist is meant to be everything the neurotic Niles is not. Despite that, or perhaps because of it, Niles and Daphne were the romantic core of the show throughout its run. Jane Leeves and David Hyde Pierce had chemistry that could drive entire episodes on its own, but Daphne also had crucial, meaningful relationships with every other character too.
 As Ted Lasso 's Keeley Jones, Juno Temple has mastered the ability to juggle romance and female friendship. Aside from Ted himself, Keeley is arguably Ted Lasso 's most important character , as her will-they/won't-they with Roy and empowering friendship with Rebecca are the driving force of two of the show's biggest storylines. Most importantly, Temple, like Daphne, knows how to be completely herself.
 Ethan Embry
 As Bob "Bulldog" Briscoe
 Ethan Embry in Grace and Frankie Season 4 Image via MovieStillsDB 
 As the loud, short-tempered, in-your-face sportscaster whose radio show followed Frasier's, Bulldog seemed at first like little more than a one-note bit character. Even in just his short bursts on screen, however, Dan Butler imbued the character with a surprising tenderness beneath his bravado that earned him a meaningful appearance in all of Frasier 's 11 seasons .
 As one of the adopted children of Frankie and Sol's already-eccentric relationship, Grace and Frankie 's Coyote Bergstein faced a similar challenge. Yet Ethan Embry played Coyote's struggles with a sincerity that was both comedic and endearing. The character quickly became more than simply a symbol of Frankie and Sol's unusual family, just as Bulldog outgrew his character's original constraints.
 Edi Patterson
 As Bebe Glazer
 Judy (Edi Patterson) looking upset while taking a bubble bath in The Righteous Gemstones Season 4 Ep 8 Image via Max
 Ruthless and flirtatious in an unnerving kind of way, the appearance of Frasier's agent always promised a darkly chaotic payoff. Harriet Sansom Harris embodied the mischievous twinkle in Bebe's eye that made the character's sense of danger immediately apparent. Still, as someone working in Frasier's best interest, Bebe had a compelling, anti-hero-like quality to her.
 Ruthless and unnervingly flirtatious is a specific yet perfectly apt description of Edi Patterson's role in The Righteous Gemstones ​​​​​​. Easily the most intimidating and unpredictable of the Gemstone siblings , Judy also had a lively sex life with her boyfriend that left little to the imagination. Patterson has brought this unique energy to shows like Vice Principals and Abbott Elementary , and it's a perfect fit for Bebe.
 Dan Levy
 As Gil Chesterton
 David looks shocked while sitting at the table in Schitt's Creek MovieStillsDB 
 Dan Levy would bring a fresh take on Gil Chesterton, originally played by the British Edward Hibbert. However, the Schitt's Creek star is certainly capable of harnessing a campy snootiness that rivals Frasier's own. In some ways, the role would actually further Schitt's Creek 's endeavor to challenge assumptions about people's sexuality, as Gil is thought to be gay throughout Frasier , but notoriously isn't.
 As the radio station's resident restaurant critic, the role would give Levy, who has created and hosted a cooking show, the opportunity to lean into his own interests and personal opinions. The more outlandish those opinions are, the more they would actually suit the character. Ultimately, Levy's presence would bring a comedic and intentional voice to Frasier that would highlight what first made the show special.
